title: Execution-route hasher with online latency calibration
creator: Ava Patel
description: Goal: Build a lightweight execution-route hashing mechanism that groups inference requests by tensor topology (seq length distribution, head count, batch shape, kv cache behavior) and GPU family, and combine that with an online latency calibration model so the runtime can pick near-optimal kernels without full profiling for every new traffic pattern. Background: Current kernel picking either uses coarse heuristics or expensive microprobes. For tail latency-sensitive workloads we need faster decisions that still respect architecture and seq-length topology. The approach uses a locality-preserving hash over request features (sequence length percentiles, head/dim ratios, kv-cache hit patterns, batch size) to map requests to execution buckets, attach a lightweight calibration estimator per bucket that learns mean/variance of end-to-end QPS/latency for candidate kernels, and pick the kernel with lowest predicted P99 subject to throughput constraints. This ticket scopes the runtime components, calibration algorithm, and safe rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end implementation in the runtime that computes execution-route hash for each request and records feature fingerprints to metrics
Online calibration model returns per-bucket latency estimates within 15% of observed P50/P95 on our benchmark suite after 2k requests
Fallback policy in place: if bucket has <50 samples, use fast-lookup heuristic or a conservative kernel choice
A/B experiment showing >=6% token-cost reduction or >=10% median latency improvement on mixed seq-len traffic for at least two GPU families
PRs merged for runtime changes and unit/integration tests added; canary rollout configured via console route policy

implementation_notes: Hash: 64-bit Murmur3 variant seeded by GPU SKU. Features: seq length percentiles (10th/50th/90th), batch size, kv-hit-ratio estimate, attention head count, embedding dim bucketed. Calibration: per-bucket EW-Bayes linear model with sample-count threshold and pseudo-count prior. Storage: bounded LRU bucket table per worker with TTL and periodic aggregation to per-GPU stats for Console. Rollout: feature gate at route level, safe fallback to existing heuristic when bucket is cold or estimator variance high.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Bad hashing could over-shard samples leading to noisy estimates; mitigate by adaptive merge of low-count adjacent buckets. Risk: GPU-specific performance cliffs; mitigate via GPU-SKU tags and mandatory A/B on targeted SKUs. Risk: metric overhead; mitigate by sampling 10% of requests for detailed traces and aggregating the rest.
next_steps: 1) Merge prototype PR after addressing hash eviction bug (PR #492). 2) Add Console metrics endpoints and dashboard tiles. 3) Run 2-week internal canary on staging with mixed synthetic and replayed production traces. 4) If stable, schedule customer canary on dedicated non-critical customers.
